audits.title: 160 A CLOSED-LOOP AUDIT EXAMINING THE USE OF PROPHYLACTIC ANTI-COAGULATION IN OLDER ADULTS ADMITTED TO A SPECIALIST GERIATRIC SERVICE
audits.standard: Prophylactic anticoagulation for all hospitalised older adults unless contraindicated; target 95%
audits.setting: Medicine for the elderly service, Connolly Hospital, Dublin (level 3 hospital)

cycle1.result: 80% of older adults admitted were receiving prophylactic anticoagulation.

audits.intervention: Cause and effect analysis then small tests of change over 4 PDSA cycles addressing history taking, clinician education, documentation, handover, medication reconciliation and pharmacy support

cycle2.result: 98.1% (104/106) receiving prophylactic anticoagulation; 83% after one month.

audits.other_findings: Only 2 patients lacked documentation of a reason for not prescribing.
audits.citation: Brar S, Sheehan O, Martin R, Rasheed M. 160 A CLOSED-LOOP AUDIT EXAMINING THE USE OF PROPHYLACTIC ANTI-COAGULATION IN OLDER ADULTS ADMITTED TO A SPECIALIST GERIATRIC SERVICE. Age and Ageing. 2022;51(Supplement_3). doi:10.1093/ageing/afac218.136.

audits.title: Improved use of thromboprophylaxis for deep vein thrombosis following an educational intervention.
audits.setting: Medical wards, SUNY Downstate Medical Center, Brooklyn (teaching hospital)

cycle1.result: 47% received any prophylaxis; 43% received appropriate prophylaxis.

audits.intervention: Regular education, a decision support tool and regular audit and feedback to residents.

cycle2.result: Any prophylaxis 86% at 12 months, maintained at 18 months; appropriate prophylaxis 68% at 12 months and 85% at 18 months.

audits.citation: Cohn SL, Adekile A, Mahabir V. Improved use of thromboprophylaxis for deep vein thrombosis following an educational intervention. J Hosp Med. 2006;1(6):331-338. doi:10.1002/jhm.137. PMID: 17219525.

audits.title: Innovative approaches to increase deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis rate resulting in a decrease in hospital-acquired deep vein thrombosis at a tertiary-care teaching hospital.
audits.setting: Department of Medicine, Kings County Hospital Center, tertiary teaching hospital

cycle1.result: DVT prophylaxis rate on the general medicine house-staff service 63%; 14 hospital-acquired DVTs (2.6 per 1000 discharges, 95% CI 1.5-4.4).

audits.intervention: Layered, multifaceted programme from November 2002: provider education, provider reminders with decision support, and audit with feedback.

cycle2.result: DVT prophylaxis rate 96%; 1 hospital-acquired DVT (0.2 per 1000 discharges, 95% CI 0.0-1.1), P = .007.

audits.citation: Bullock-Palmer RP, Weiss S, Hyman C. Innovative approaches to increase deep vein thrombosis prophylaxis rate resulting in a decrease in hospital-acquired deep vein thrombosis at a tertiary-care teaching hospital. J Hosp Med. 2008;3(2):148-155. doi:10.1002/jhm.291. PMID: 18438791.

audits.title: Audit of anticoagulant thromboprophylaxis in hospitalized oncology patients.
audits.standard: 2004 American College of Chest Physicians consensus guidelines on VTE prophylaxis
audits.setting: Christchurch Hospital Oncology Service inpatients; cross-sectional chart review over two 4-week periods

cycle1.result: 38/113 (33.6%) had indications for prophylactic anticoagulation; 23 of these had contraindications, leaving 15 (13%) appropriate; only one was appropriately given prophylaxis.

audits.other_findings: Authors suggest local promotion of VTE prophylaxis to improve uptake.
audits.citation: Chin PK, Beckert LE, Gunningham S, Edwards AL, Robinson BA. Audit of anticoagulant thromboprophylaxis in hospitalized oncology patients. Intern Med J. 2009;39(12):819-825. doi:10.1111/j.1445-5994.2008.01828.x. PMID: 19220527.

audits.title: Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis guideline implementation is improved by nurse directed feedback and audit.
audits.standard: Australian and New Zealand Working Party on the Management and Prevention of VTE recommendations

cycle1.result: 37.9% of high-risk patients received appropriate thromboprophylaxis (82.2% were high risk).

cycle2.result: 54.1% of high-risk patients received appropriate prophylaxis (absolute improvement 16%; 95% CI 11.7%, 20.5%; OR 1.96, 1.62-2.37).

audits.other_findings: 81.0% of audit 2 patients were high risk.
audits.citation: Gibbs H, Fletcher J, Blombery P, Collins R, Wheatley D. Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis guideline implementation is improved by nurse directed feedback and audit. Thromb J. 2011;9(1):7. doi:10.1186/1477-9560-9-7. PMID: 21466681.

audits.standard: Optimal DVT prophylaxis for hospitalised medical patients

audits.other_findings: Improvement sustained at 95% on chart review 1 year after implementation.

audits.title: Bridging efforts to longitudinally improve and evaluate VEnous thromboembolism prophylaxis uptake in hospitalized cancer patients through Interprofessional Teamwork (BELIEVE IT): a study by Princess Margaret Cancer Centre.
audits.standard: Institutional VTE prophylaxis guidelines and policy
audits.setting: Princess Margaret Cancer Centre, Toronto, inpatients with solid tumours

cycle1.result: 11 of 57 (19.3%) eligible patients received appropriate pharmacological prophylaxis.

audits.intervention: Guidelines and institutional policy, educational in-services for physicians, nurses and pharmacists, and Cancer Quality Committee engagement.

cycle2.result: 96.7% prophylaxis rate, maintained ten weeks later.

audits.other_findings: Intermediate audits: 46.5% of 185 after 2009 policy and teaching; average 62.3% across three 2011 audits. Minimal bleeding observed.
audits.citation: Seki JT, Vather T, Atenafu EG, Kukreti V, Krzyzanowska MK. Bridging efforts to longitudinally improve and evaluate VEnous thromboembolism prophylaxis uptake in hospitalized cancer patients through Interprofessional Teamwork (BELIEVE IT): a study by Princess Margaret Cancer Centre. Thromb Res. 2014;133(1):34-41. doi:10.1016/j.thromres.2013.10.025. PMID: 24210735.

audits.title: Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in acute medical admissions to a university teaching hospital.
audits.setting: Acute medical admissions, St James' Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: 104 of 265 (39%) at-risk patients prescribed appropriate thromboprophylaxis.

audits.intervention: Hospital-wide educational initiatives and a new drug prescription chart.

cycle2.result: 108 of 188 (57%) at-risk patients prescribed appropriate thromboprophylaxis.

audits.other_findings: Over 40% of at-risk patients still did not receive thromboprophylaxis.
audits.citation: Lyons O, Loh J, Lim M, O'Riordan D, Silke B. Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in acute medical admissions to a university teaching hospital. Ir Med J. 2013;106(8):235-238. PMID: 24282892.

audits.title: Pharmacological thromboprophylaxis in elderly medical inpatients: Lessons from a local audit in the era of NEJM Evidence.
audits.setting: Large Australian tertiary institution (Alfred Health), Melbourne

cycle1.result: Excellent guideline adherence; about 10% ambulant patients given prophylaxis outside guideline criteria; 2 VTE (1.4%) and 5 minor bleeds (3.5%).

audits.citation: Bortz H, Melone O, Chee A. Pharmacological thromboprophylaxis in elderly medical inpatients: Lessons from a local audit in the era of NEJM Evidence. Intern Med J. 2026;56(4):714-717. doi:10.1111/imj.70333. PMID: 41626648.

audits.title: [Preventive treatment of thrombosis: audit on heparin prescription].
audits.standard: National guidelines matching heparin prescription to thrombotic risk; platelet monitoring protocol

cycle1.result: 52.2% correct regimen, 4.4% underprescribed and 43.4% overprescribed; platelet monitoring protocol respected in 44%.

audits.intervention: Results communicated to all prescribers and national guidelines diffused.

cycle2.result: 81% of doses adapted to thrombotic risk, 2% too low, 17% too high.

audits.other_findings: Platelet monitoring was insufficient in 41% and absent in 15% at baseline.
audits.citation: Aouizerate P, Mabiala H, Perrot F, Guizard M. [Preventive treatment of thrombosis: audit on heparin prescription]. Therapie. 1998;53(2):101-106. PMID: 9773108.

audits.title: Using knowledge translation for quality improvement: an interprofessional education intervention to improve thromboprophylaxis among medical inpatients.
audits.standard: Use of LMWH for VTE prophylaxis in treatment-eligible medical inpatients (target not stated)
audits.setting: Resident teaching services for general medicine inpatients, Mayo Clinic, Rochester

cycle1.result: LMWH used in 12.1% of treatment-eligible hospitalised medical patients.

audits.intervention: Several PDSA cycles of resident-of-resident and pharmacist-of-resident education with performance audit and feedback, sustained by a monthly pharmacist-led interprofessional session at resident orientation.
audits.other_findings: Pharmacist-of-resident education produced the largest improvement.
audits.citation: Myers MK, Jansson-Knodell CL, Schroeder DR, O'Meara JG, Bonnes SL, Ratelle JT. Using knowledge translation for quality improvement: an interprofessional education intervention to improve thromboprophylaxis among medical inpatients. J Multidiscip Healthc. 2018;11:467-472. doi:10.2147/jmdh.s171745. PMID: 30271162.
